why: Adding the clause‑boundary/punctuation fallback made the model prefer cuts at clear clause breaks instead of immediately after auxiliaries/finite verbs with short complements, so it fixed many short-piece mistakes (positive mean gains in the ≤3, ≤5, ≤7, ≤10 bins) by keeping short complements and multiword names together. The same change shifted some cuts earlier in longer sentences, splitting noun phrases, quoted spans, and objects (the ≤99 bin is slightly negative and several large negative tail moves show cuts inserted inside names/objects), producing localized large degradations.
lesson: A later revision should preserve the short‑segment gains from preferring clause/punctuation boundaries while avoiding moves that introduce earlier cuts which split multiword noun phrases, quoted spans, or long complements in longer sentences.
